This article examines the demographic and clinical characteristics of patients with [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] registered in the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]], specifically comparing newly diagnosed patients against prevalent patients who had a hospital contact during the reporting period [^src1]. Because the available data consists of a single cross-sectional snapshot from 2023, no temporal trends or year-over-year changes can be established [^src1]. Furthermore, the dataset does not define specific clinical targets or thresholds, meaning no met or missed goals can be evaluated [^src1].

In terms of patient volume, the database tracks 213 prevalent patients with a hospital contact, which is significantly higher than the 35 newly diagnosed patients in the same period [^src1]. Men are the clear leaders in gender distribution across both cohorts, accounting for 74% (26 patients) of the newly diagnosed group and 65% (139 patients) of the prevalent group [^src1]. Conversely, women represent the trailing demographic, making up 26% (9 patients) of new diagnoses and 35% (74 patients) of the prevalent population [^src1].

Age distributions show that prevalent patients are slightly older on average. The mean age for prevalent patients is 46 years (ranging from 17 to 88), compared to 45 years (ranging from 8 to 80) for newly diagnosed patients [^src1]. The median age follows the same pattern, sitting at 44 years for the prevalent group and 42 years for the newly diagnosed group [^src1]. An outlier in the age data is the minimum age: newly diagnosed patients include children as young as 8, whereas the youngest prevalent patient with a contact is 17 [^src1].

Regarding healthcare utilization, newly diagnosed patients require slightly more frequent contact with the hospital system. They average 11 contacts (median 10), while prevalent patients average 10 contacts (median 9) [^src1]. However, an outlier exists in the maximum number of contacts; a prevalent patient recorded up to 28 contacts, surpassing the maximum of 21 seen in the newly diagnosed cohort [^src1]. When analyzing the contact type, physical attendance is the leading method of interaction, constituting 63% (164 contacts) for new patients and 65% (729 contacts) for prevalent patients [^src1]. Virtual contacts trail behind, accounting for 37% (96 contacts) and 35% (396 contacts) respectively [^src1].
